_summary: All eight r2 findings are closed. The builder's ec4afc3d file reproduces byte-identically from the script. Stage 2 checks 1-8 pass, C29 is clean, the tier verdict is verbatim, and 186 of 186 cited register ids resolve (181 active, 5 partial, 0 tier B) with SCOPE in every consumed_by. The independent cross-check of 1,115 filing / levy / insurance facts found no in-scope filing missing. One major defect remained. The State annual-reconciliation entry put the OR household and agricultural annual returns in scope, which contradicts the US-OWN-005 deferral recorded in the same file. The auditor fixed it in place with a new out_of_scope record, and also corrected one unsupported channel claim (MA PFML 'to DOR'). Five minor findings are routed, none blocking RSPEC. The builder's related_obligations_no_return classification is accepted. Verdict PASS.

_ruling_related_obligations_no_return: ACCEPTED as a reversible builder classification. Basis: (a) nothing leaves scope: the four classes stay documented in the CCG, so no F15 descoping is involved; (b) none is a recurring authority return built from payroll data, so Stage 3 has no Report Specification to build; (c) WARN is an HR-scope notice and F19 forbids carrying it as a payroll filing; (d) the event-driven per-employee UI reports to an agency (SC UCB-113, GA DOL-402, OH mass-layoff) correctly stay in the SUI filing entry, not in this key. Registered bases re-read: 29 USC 2102 (60 days; State dislocated-worker unit and local official), IWD 'respond to IWD within 10 days', CDOR DR 0995 notice, CT UC-21 packet, GA DOL-800, NJ BC-10. The list is illustrative ('e.g.'). Equivalent items in the facts also fall in these classes: TN LB-0489, PA UC-1609, NY IA 12.3, the State POA forms CA DE 48 / CO DR 0145, and the MN/NH/SC notices. Condition: the RSPEC builder treats the four classes as rules, not as a closed list; this is recorded in B7.

findings.location: scope_manifest.json!authority_filings.in_scope[10] State annual withholding reconciliation (per State)!note (script line 192)
findings.problem: The note put 'the OR annual forms OA (household) and WA / OR-STT-A (agricultural)' inside an in-scope filing. Those are State-level returns of household and agricultural employers. The same file defers 'State-level rules for special populations' to a later round (employment_types.out_of_scope[1], US-OWN-005), so the manifest contradicted itself. Stage 3 would have built OR special-population specs but not the equivalent returns of other States (CT-941 HHE / CT-W3 HHE, DC UC-30-H, FL RT-7, GA DOL-4, LA domestic annual, all present in the CCG / RSPEC facts). The general OR annual reconciliation, Form OR-WR (US-ORS5-010), was not named. The live OR 150-211-155-2 (2026) confirms the facts: Form OA is for domestic household employers that file annually, OR-STT-A is the annual STT return of annual filers, and OR-WR carries withholding and STT.
findings.expected: Note: 'Includes the OR Form OR-WR annual reconciliation with the W-2s [US-ORS5-010]. The State annual returns of household and agricultural employers (e.g. OR Form OA, Form WA / OR-STT-A [US-ORS5-010]) are not in this entry: State-level rules for special populations are deferred to a later round (US-OWN-005); see out_of_scope.' New out_of_scope record 'State annual returns of household and agricultural employers (e.g. OR Form OA, Form WA / OR-STT-A)', descoping_reason = the US-OWN-005 sentence verbatim, register_ids [US-OWN-005, US-ORS5-010]. APPLIED in build_scope_manifest.py and regenerated.
findings.evidence: OR DOR 150-211-155-2 (2026) fetched 2026-11-03 (pypdf): 'Domestic household employers ... may file ... annually using Form OA Domestic'; 'If you file annually, you will file Form OR-STT-A'; 'Form OR-WR (which includes state withholding and the STT)'. CCG P4138 / T764 and RSPEC fact rspec.or.annual.forms carry the same forms; facts rspec.ct.household.forms [US-CTS5-014], rspec.dc.ui_qtr.form, rspec.fl.other_forms, rspec.ga.ui_qtr.form, rspec.la.ui_qtr.due.

findings.problem: The note read 'MA PFML (quarterly contribution return to DOR ...) [US-MAS5-012]'. The cited row and its registered page say employers 'must send to DFML a contribution of 0.88% of eligible wages', and nothing in US-MAS5-012 names DOR. Agent 2 closes ma.report.pfml.quarterly (DFML 'Wage contributions & reporting for PFML'), then the builder may name the channel.

findings.location: scope_manifest.json!authority_filings.in_scope[5] SSA Forms W-2 / W-3 (and W-2c corrections)!format; option_mapper_scope._correction_codes_basis
findings.problem: The text says 'W-2c in EFW2C, Pub. 42-014' and cites US-FIL-002, but US-FIL-002's figure_or_rule_carried carries only 'EFW2 Publication 42-007'. No active cited row carries 'EFW2C' or '42-014'. US-FEDP52-013 does carry it, but that row is gated. The registered ssa.gov page returns 403 to WebFetch (r2 and r3). The rule itself was verified: the SSA EFW2 TY2026 publication (US-FEDS5-032 document) refers to the 'Correction (EFW2C) file format' for W-2c. The identifier 42-014 was not verified.
findings.expected: Agent 2 widens US-FIL-002 figure_or_rule_carried to 'EFW2 Publication 42-007 and EFW2C Publication 42-014 for tax year 2026' from the registered page (Chrome read) or a saved local copy. Until then the builder cites US-FEDS5-032 for 'W-2c in EFW2C' and keeps '42-014' only once a cited row carries it.
findings.evidence: Register rows US-FIL-002 (active, EFW2 only), US-FEDP52-013 (gated, 'EFW2C Publication 42-014'), US-WIS5-015 (active, WI DOR: 'W-2C = EFW2C (Pub 42-014)'); 00-official-sources/ccg-sources/FED/FED_SSA_EFW2_TY2026_Pub42-007_2026-11-02.pdf.

findings.problem: Three of the five cited 'partial' register rows are not flagged where they are cited, unlike US-FEDS5-031 and US-FEDS5-012. US-GAS5-020 is GDOL proposed-rule text, and its adopted text and effective date were not read. It is the only basis for 'the GA mass-separation report ... part of this obligation'. US-WYP9W-001 has no 2026 factor values in the statute. US-CAS5-017 does not state the eCPR thresholds.
findings.expected: Append a partial-row flag at each citation, worded like the 941 entry: 'US-GAS5-020 is a partial register row (GDOL proposed rule; adopted text not read)'; '(US-WYP9W-001 partial: 2026 factor values not in statute)'; '(US-CAS5-017 partial: eCPR thresholds not stated)'. Through build_scope_manifest.py.

findings.problem: The sealed MANDATE employer_payroll_levies row (line 52) names the WV unemployment automation and administration fee from 2026-07-01 [US-WVS5-002, active A.1]. The 21-State enumeration in the label's basis omits it, and US-WVS5-002 is not cited anywhere in the manifest. The fee is an annual bill ('billed by March 31, delinquent 30 days later'), not an item on the quarterly UI return, so the SUI note's statement that 'The UI return carries the State UI-linked ... levies' is wrong for WV. The figure itself is an open CCG item (wv.ui.sb1053_fee).
findings.expected: Add to the basis: 'WV unemployment automation and administration fee from 2026-07-01, annual, billed by WorkForce WV by March 31 (figure open: CCG wv.ui.sb1053_fee) US-WVS5-002'. Change the SUI note to 'The UI return carries the State UI-linked levies except where a levy is billed separately (WV annual fee [US-WVS5-002])'. Agent 2 appends ';SCOPE' to US-WVS5-002 consumed_by in the same pass.
findings.evidence: MANDATE.md line 52; register US-WVS5-002 figure_or_rule_carried; _research/CCG-annex_WV-facts.json unresolved wv.ui.sb1053_fee.

findings.location: scope_manifest.json!authority_filings.in_scope[13] Local income / wage tax returns and in_scope[14] City employer payroll taxes!register_ids and note
findings.problem: Two returns appear in two in-scope entries. The Jersey City and Newark employer payroll-tax returns are listed in both entries. The St. Louis earnings tax (local entry) and payroll expense tax (city entry) share one return: the registered page says 'Employers must file both taxes together quarterly, using Forms W-10/P-10' [US-MOP52-006]. _in_scope_note says the Report Specifications 'must cover every filing above', so Stage 3 could build two specs for one return, or count one return twice in the Report Matrix.
findings.expected: Add to _in_scope_note: 'One Report Specification per authority return: Jersey City and Newark payroll-tax returns are specified under the city employer entry; the St. Louis W-10/P-10 is one return carrying the earnings tax and the payroll expense tax [US-MOP52-006]; the local entry cross-references these.'

findings.location: 01-ccg/US-CCG-001-v1.0.docx!FED.15 Special populations!P1047 (and MULTI.15 Special populations P1117)
findings.problem: Scope wording drifts across artifacts (P4.3). FED.15 reads 'All special populations are in scope. Federal rules are below; State rules are in the State annexes.' MULTI.15 reads 'All other special populations follow the State annexes of the States the routing selects.' Both contradict the US-OWN-005 sentence used verbatim in CCG m01 P32, m11.3 P727 and scope_manifest.json, which says State-level rules are deferred. State annex rows such as OR T764 r1-r2, CT P1650 and FL P1826/P1852 document the household and agricultural returns with no deferral marker. A downstream builder reading the annexes alone would treat them as in scope.
findings.expected: FED.15 P1047 and MULTI.15 P1117 open with CC.POPULATIONS_SENTENCE verbatim ('All special employee populations are in scope at the federal layer (owner decision US-OWN-005); State-level rules for special populations are deferred to a later round (US-OWN-005).'). State-annex special-population rows carry '(State-level rule documented for information; deferred, US-OWN-005; no Report Specification this round)'. Fix at the next CCG touch; RSPEC is not blocked because scope_manifest.json now records the deferral.
